GROUND RULES: Contestants who choose to enter the Legacy Steer Roping event must be at least 50 years old or a permit holder at the time of entry closing. They must also be entered in the steer roping event at the Steer Roping Event in Abilene. To be eligible, the contestant must not have been an NFSR qualifier during the past three years. Permit members of all ages will also be eligible to enter.

Contestants will pay entry fees of $300. Contestants will not compete on any additional steers. The times that are recorded for the contestants' competition runs at the Steer Roping Event in Abilene will be used to determine the pay-off. Pay-off will only include the entry fees for the contestants who entered the Legacy Steer Roping through PROCOM. 6% will be held out of the total amount for the PRCA prior to the pay-off. Only the three go-rounds and the average after three go-rounds will be included in the pay-off for the Legacy Steer Roping. There will be no additional added money and since no additional animals will be run, there will be no additional stock charge or PROCOM charge.

Money won in the Legacy Steer Roping will not count towards PRCA World Standings, circuit standings, All Around standings, or for money won qualifications. It will count towards qualifying for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals held in conjunction with the National Finals Steer Roping. (NFSR qualifiers will not be eligible for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals).
STK CONT.: Various

detailLines: Weyburn SK CN NPP
June 2
Outlaw Buckers & Oil Kings Bronc Match
ARENA: Weyburn Agricultural Society
ADDRESS: 7B Prairie Ave. W
PERFS: 1 Perf: June 2- 4:00 PM
EVENTS: SB @ $30000
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES: SB-$150
PERMITS: SB
GROUND RULES: ALL CONTESTANTS - May also enter online at www.rodeocanada.com between May 13 at 8 AM and May 14 at 2 PM.
All Contestants: Re-entries, if needed, will be accepted for available positions 48 hours after entries close from 8am-2pm. See Rodeo Entry Information on Rodeo Schedule.

QUALIFICATIONS: Maximum 30 contestants based on top 100 blended CPRA/PRCA standing as of Monday 13,2024 will be used to determine draw outs. If the qualifications are not filled by contestants with dollars won leaving open positions; the remaining openings will be filled by a random draw of card holders then semi-pro card holders. If there are still open positions, all remaining openings will be filled by a random draw of permit holders.

FORMAT: One go-round with a Top eight (8) will advance to finals. If there are not eight (8) qualified rides during the long go, all remaining positions will be filled by random draw. If the 8th place is tied going into the finals, the tie will be broken by highest marked spur ride from the long go, if still tied spots will be determined by random draw.
PAYOUT: 50% of the total purse for the long go and 50% for the short go. Long Go will pay 8 places and Short Go will pay 4 places - 40%, 30%, 20%, 10%. There will be no average payout.

TURN OUT/ALTERNATE PROCEDURE: Contestants who have originally entered and were eligible at time of entry but were drawn out will be added to an alternate list. These contestants will be notified of any turn-outs or doctor releases and be given the option of re-entry up to 24 hours prior to rodeo turn out deadline, any turnouts done after the alternate time frame will be filled by walk up replacements only. If stock has already been drawn in the rough stock they will draw stock from a pool of animals consisting of all turned out stock for that performance.

Walk Up Replacements: Contestants who have originally entered and were eligible at time of entry but were drawn out may, in person, check with the rodeo secretary no later than 1 hour prior to the performance to confirm their availability and desire to be an alternate. If selected, by random draw of all walk ups available, an alternate will assume the competition position of the contestant that he is replacing, in the rough stock they will draw stock from a pool of animals consisting of all turned out stock for that performance.

Re-entries: Re-entries will be accepted where the actual entries accepted during the original entry period were less than the limit. Entries be re-opened sometime prior to the riding event stock draw. Contestants that enter during the re-entry period will be placed in the remaining available positions (available positions will be defined by the stock contractor and/or committee based on the number of contestants that entered during the re-entry period). All re-entries will be accepted to fill the performances not to exceed the original limit defined in the ground rules (based on "money won" qualifications).

If a contestant notifies a turn-out, DR or visible release and is replaced by an alternate, the alternate contestant will be responsible for the entry fees. If the contestant that notified the turnout or visible release is not replaced by an alternate, they will be responsible for the entry fee. If a contestant properly doctor releases they will not be responsible for entry fees.
Entry Fees: SB: $150
+CRES & other associate fees with be charged in addition to all entry fees as per the rule book.

NOTE: Money won at this event will count towards the Xbroncs Standings. Money won at this event will count towards qualification for the 2026 National finals Rodeo and the 2026 Rookie of the Year Standings as long as the contestant competed at a minimum of 40 PRCA rodeos during the 2026 Rodeo year. Money won at this event will not count towards All Around Standings.
STK CONT.: Outlawbuckers Rodeo

Turn outs and doctor's releases in the Qualifying Performance will be replaced by alternates from the alternate list based on 2026 PRCA World Standings. An alternate will be placed in the position corresponding with the contestant that he is replacing. If stock has already been drawn, he will receive the stock drawn for the contestant that he is replacing. Turn outs and doctor's release in the Darby Extreme BB Event on June 7 will be replaced by the next highest ranked contestant (based on scores) from the Qualifying Performance on June 6. A contestant will not be accepted as an entry at this event if he is already placed in a position at another PRCA Rodeo or event that has a "same performance" conflict as this event.
GRACE PERIOD: Will expire one hour after entries close.

QUALIFICATIONS: 40 minimum entries based on 2026 PRCA World Standings as of 7 days prior to entry closing. A contestant who has been accepted as an entry at the Darby Extreme Bareback event on Sunday, June 7, will not be accepted as an entry for the Qualifier on Saturday, June 6. The top 10 from the Qualifying Performance on June 6 will advance to the Darby Extreme Bareback event on June 7.

FORMAT for the Qualifying Performance on Sat., June 6: One go-round if 31 to 40 entries. One go-round with a top 10 finals if 21 to 30 entries. Two go-rounds if 20 or less entries. The top 10 in the average will advance to the Darby Extreme Bareback event on Sun., June 7. If ties result in more than 10 to advance (will not exceed 10), the tied contestant with the single highest score in either go-round will advance. If still tied, the tied contestant with the highest ranking in 2026 World Standings (as of 7 days prior to entry closing) will advance. If a contestant does not accept advancement to the Extreme event due to injury or any other reason, the contestant with the next highest ranking in the average from the Qualifier will advance.
ENTRY FEES: $100 (plus $35 supplemental fee) The contestants who advance from the Qualifying Performance to the Extreme event will not be required to pay any additional fees.

PAY-OFF for the Qualifying Performance on Sat., June 6. Eight places will be paid in the average (There will be no payoff for the finals or go-rounds if two go-rounds or if one go-round and a finals. Percentages paid for placings will be in accordance with the rulebook (R5.4.1).

NOTE: This event will count for qualification for the 2026 National Finals Rodeo and the 2026 Rookie of the Year Standings as long as the contestant has competed at a minimum of 40 PRCA rodeos during the 2026 rodeo year. Money won at this event will not count towards All Around or Circuit Standings nor will the event be applied to a contestant's required circuit participation count.
STK CONT.: Various

detailLines: Darby MT NPP
June 7
Dutton Ranch Darby Xtreme Bareback
ARENA: Richard Cromwell Arena
ADDRESS: 200 Rodeo Rd,
PERFS: 1 Perf: June 7- 3:00 PM
EVENTS: BB @ $50000
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES: BB-$250
PERMITS: BB

GROUND RULES: ALL CONTESTANTS - Contestants who turn-out or doctor's release the Darby Extreme Bareback event on June 7 will be replaced by the next highest ranking on the alternate list for the Extreme event which will be based on highest scores in the average from the Qualifying Performance on June 6.
GRACE PERIOD: Will expire one hour after entries close.

QUALIFICATIONS: 30 entries will be accepted for the Darby Extreme Bareback event on Sun., June 7. The top 20 who enter based on 2026 PRCA World Standings (as of 7 days prior to entry closing) will be accepted as entries for the Darby Extreme Bareback event on Sunday, June 7. Ten contestants will advance from the Qualifying Performance on Saturday, June 6 to the Extreme event on Sunday, June 7. If less than 20 contestants enter the Darby Extreme Bareback event on June 7, remaining available positions will be filled from contestants advancing from the Qualifying performance based on highest scores (not to exceed a total of 30).

FORMAT FOR THE QUALIFYING PERFORMANCE: The Qualifying Performance will be either one go-round, two go-rounds, or one go-round with progressive round depending on the number of entries. If one go-round, the contestants with ten highest scores in the Qualifying Performance will advance to the Extreme Event (will not exceed ten). If ties result in more than ten to advance, the tied contestant(s) with the highest ranking in the 2026 World Standings (as of 7 days prior to entry closing) will advance. If two go-rounds or one go-round with a progressive round or a finals, the ten contestants with the highest rankings in the average after two go-rounds will advance to Extreme event. If ties result in more than ten to advance, the tied contestant with the single highest score in the Qualifying Performance will advance. If a contestant does not accept advancement to the Extreme event due to injury in the Qualifying performance or any other reason, the contestant with the next highest ranking in the average from the Qualifying performance will advance. Ten contestants will advance.

FORMAT FOR THE EXTREME EVENT: One go-round with a top 12 finals. The 30 contestants will be placed into 3 sections with 10 contestants in each section. Contestants, who enter, based on their rankings in the 2026 World Standings (as of 7 days prior to entry closing) will be placed in the section as follows: Section one: 1, 6, 7, 12, 13, 18, 19 and 1st, 4th, and 9th from the Qualifying Performance. Section two: 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, and 2nd, 5th, and 8th from the Qualifying Performance. Section three: 3, 4, 9, 10, 15, 16, and 3rd, 6th, 7th, and 10th from the Qualifying Performance. Contestants ranking will be dependent on the contestants who enter. For example, if the contestant who is ranked 1st in the standings does not enter, and the contestant who is ranked 2nd does enter, the contestant who is ranked 2nd in the standings will fill the #1 position since he was the highest ranked contestant who actually entered. After the contestants have been placed in the three sections, PROCOM will draw a random order for the contestants within each section to be listed on the judges sheets. The top 4 contestants based on highest scores from each of the three sections will advance to the finals. If ties result in more than 4 to advance, see following tie breaker procedure. If there are less than 4 qualified rides in a section, the contestant with the next highest score from the other sections who is not already advancing, will advance to fill that position.

TIE BREAKER PROCEDURE - Prior to the event, the judges will randomly draw a number (1 through 30) for each of the 30 contestants. This number will be used to break any ties for advancement to the finals. For example, if 4th place in a section is tied between two contestants, and one contestant's drawn number is #1 and the other contestant's drawn number is #12, the contestant with the lowest number which in the example is #1, will advance to the finals.

TURN-OUT, DR's and VIR's in the Darby Extreme Bareback event on Sunday will be replaced by contestants from the alternate list. If the Qualifying Performance is one go-round, the order of the alternate list will be based on highest single scores in the Qualifying Performance. If the Qualifying Performance is two go-rounds or one go-round with a progressive or a finals, the alternate list will be based on highest rankings in the average. Contestants who desire to be used as alternates must check-in with the rodeo secretary no later than one hour prior to the start of the Extreme event. After the one hour check-in deadline, the alternates will be randomly drawn to the available positions. If stock has already been drawn the alternate contestant will compete on the animal that has been drawn by the contestant that he is replacing.
DRAFT PROCESS - Will be used to assign stock to contestants. The draft process will occur at the rodeo secretary's office (or location still to be determined) 2 hours prior to the start of the event.

STOCK DRAW FOR THREE SECTIONS: There will be 12 horses set for each section with 10 contestants in each section. In order listed on the judges sheets, each contestant will draw a number, 1 through 10. The contestant who draws #1 will be the first to select an animal on which he will compete. Contestants will select their competition animals in order of the numbers that they draw. If a contestant is not physically present to select his animal, he will be moved to the bottom of the draw order. After all contestants who are present has selected their competition animals, the judges will draw animals for the contestants who are not present from the remaining animals not yet selected. The two animals not selected will become the re-rides. A coin flip will determine which will be the first re-ride. This procedure will be followed for all three sections. The time and location of the draft process will be included in PROCOM callbacks.

STOCK DRAW FOR THE FINALS: The buck order of the horses to be used in the finals will be established prior to the stock draw. The draw order will be based on scores in the long go-round. The contestant with the highest score in the long go-round will draw first and the contestant with the lowest score in the long go-round will draw last. If there are ties in the placings advancing to the finals, the tie breaker procedure will be used to determine the order in which the tied contestants draw. The competition order will be based on pre-established buck order of the horses.

ENTRY FEES: Entry fees for the 20 contestants who are originally accepted as entries for the Darby Extreme Bareback event on June 7 will be $250 (plus $35 supplemental fee).Entry fees for contestants accepted as entries for the Qualifying Performance will be $100 (plus $35 supplemental fee). The $100 entry fees for the Qualifying performance will be included in the pay-off for the Qualifying performance. The contestants who advance from the Qualifying Performance to the Darby Extreme Bareback event will not be required to pay any additional fees.

PAY-OFF for the DARBY EXTREME BAREBACK EVENT on Sun., June 7: $50,000 added plus $5,000 in entry fees for 20 contestants minus $3,300 for the 6% equals $51,700 to be included in the pay-off. $5,000 will be allotted to each of the three sections ($15,000 total), each section will pay $2,000 for 1st; $1,500 for 2nd; $1,000 for 3rd; and $500 for 4th. The remaining $36,700 will be paid out for the finals (the amount allotted for the finals may vary slightly due to doctor's released contestants who are not replaced. There will be no average pay-off. The finals will pay 6 places. The percentages paid for the 6 places will be in accordance with the Rulebook (R5.4.1).

NOTE: This event will count for qualification for the 2026 National Finals Rodeo and the 2026 Rookie of the Year Standings as long as the contestant has competed at a minimum of 40 PRCA rodeos during the 2026 rodeo year. Money won at this event will not count towards All Around or Circuit Standings nor will the event be applied to a contestant's required circuit participation count.
STK CONT.: Various
SUB. CONT.: Pickett Pro Rodeo Co. , J Bar J, Legacy Pro Rodeo LLC

If there are still remaining open positions, they will be filled by a random draw of permit holders.

FORMAT: One go-round with a top 8 finals. If there are not 8 qualified rides during the long go-round, all remaining positions will be filled by random draw. If 8th place is tied going into the finals, the tie will be broken by the highest marked spur ride from the long go-round. If still tied, the tie will be broken by random draw.

WALK-UP REPLACEMENT: Contestants who have originally entered and were eligible at time of entry but were drawn out may, in person, check with the rodeo secretary no later than 1 hour prior to the performance to confirm their availability and desire to be an alternate. If selected, by random draw of all walk-ups available, an alternate will assume the competition position of the contestant that he is replacing. In the rough stock, they will draw stock from a pool of animals consisting of all turned-out stock for the performance and all re-ride stock for that performance.

**If a contestant notifies a turn-out, DR or visible release and is replaced by an alternate, the alternate contestant will be responsible for the entry fees. If the contestant that notified the turnout or visible release is not replaced by an alternate, they will be responsible for the entry fee. If a contestant properly doctor releases they will not be responsible for entry fees.**

NOTE: Money won at Xtreme Broncs Events will count towards X-Broncs Standings which will be used for qualifying for the finale in Rapid City. In order for money won in the Wildwood Saddle Bronc competition to count for the 2026 National Finals Rodeo or the 2026 Rookie of the Year standings, during the 2026 season, a contestant must have entered and competed at a minimum of 40 PRCA rodeos. Money won at the Wildwood Saddle Bronc competition will not count towards All-Around standings.

RIDING EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Fri., June 5 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM.

TIMED EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Wed., June 10 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM. Contestants who are placed in the performances will be allowed to trade their second go-round positions with contestants who are placed in other performances. Contestants will not be allowed to trade from a performance to the slack. The rodeo secretary will post the trade deadline in the rodeo office.
TE - If a timed event animal escapes or a re-run is awarded for any other reason during a performance, the extra will be used. Only escaped animals go back into herd.
TR - Only two loops allowed.

TD, SW, TR FORMAT - Two go-rounds plus a top 12 finals. All contestants will run their first go-round in the slack. The top 50 based on fastest times from the first go-round will be placed in the first 5 performances and the remaining contestants will run their second go-round in reverse order of the first go-round in slack, following the completion of the first go-round. If there are less than 50 qualified times in the first go-round, the remaining available positions in the performances (not to exceed 50) will be filled by the contestants with no qualified times in the first go-round based on the placement order for the second go-round. If ties result in more than 50 to be placed in the performances, a random draw will determine which of the tied contestants will be placed in the performances (will not exceed 50). Placement in the performances will be in accordance with R2.6 of the PRCA Rulebook (pertaining to progressive go-rounds). Contestants who are placed in the performances will not be allowed to trade to the slack. Contestants will be allowed to trade from one performance to a different performance, up to 5 PM the day prior to the 1st performance.

ALL EVENTS - If a contestant who qualifies for the Finals notifies a turn-out, doctors release, or a visible injury release through PROCOM, the constant with the next highest ranking in the average may be contacted by Procom and placed in that available position. Non-notified turn-outs and visible injury releases after the turn-out deadline will not be replaced. If the next highest ranked contestant is not available to accept the position the next highest ranked contestant may be contacted and placed in that position. This procedure will be followed until all positions are filled. The replacement contestant's competition order will be based on his ranking in the average (not on the ranking of the contestant that he is replacing). In riding events, if an animal has already been drawn for a contestant who has turned-out, the replacement contestant will draw an animal from a pool consisting of all animals that have been turned-out (includes DR's and VIR's).
GB - Approved for first slack event in accordance with R4.9.4.

SLACK ORDER - Sunday, June 14 at 7:00 AM: GB (1st go-round), Breakaway (1st Go-round), TD (1st go-round with the exception of approximately 30 contestants that will compete during Monday's slack), Breakaway (2nd go-round), SW (approximately 50% of the 1st go-round. Monday, June 15 at 7:00 AM: TR (1st go-round), TD (finish 1st go-round with about 30 contestants), SW (finish the second half of the 1st go-round), TD (2nd go-round), GB (2nd go-round). Tuesday, June 16 at 8:30 AM: TR (2nd go-round), SW (2nd go-round).
QUALIFICATIONS: BB - 60 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. W/F's (12) $5,000 held out for finals.
SB - 70 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. W/F's (12) $5,000 held out for finals.
BR - 80 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. W/F's (12) $5,000 held out for finals. There may be two sections.
TD, SW, TR - 110 minimum entries.

QUALIFICATIONS: 30 minimum entries. No exemptions. The top 20 in the World standings (as of 7 day prior to entry closing) who enter will be accepted. Five will qualify from the Will Rogers Stampede in Claremore, OK and five will qualify from the 101 Wild West Rodeo in Ponca City, OK. These ten contestants (five from Claremore and five from Ponca City) will include the contestants with the fastest time from each of the three go-rounds from both Claremore and Ponca City who enter and who are not already qualified as entries for Pawhuska. If a go-round is tied, the tied contestant with the highest ranking in the average after three go-rounds will be accepted. If still tied, the tied contestant with the highest ranking in the 2026 World standings will be accepted. The top two contestants based on fastest times in the average after three go-rounds at both Claremore and Ponca City who enter and who are not already qualified for Pawhuska will also be accepted as entries for Pawhuska. If ties result in more than two to be accepted, the tied contestant with the single fastest time from any of the three go-rounds will be accepted.

FORMAT: Three go-rounds plus a top 12 finals. The steers used in the finals may be different steer than the steers used in the other go-rounds. Extras will be used to replace sick or injured animals. The misdraw procedure will not be used. There will be a hand pulled barrier with a 30 ft score. In the case of inclement weather, the event may be moved to the indoor arena on site. If moved, the score will be one foot less than the length of the box. $80 stock charge per go-round.

NOTE: Contestants are required to go to a minimum of 15 PRCA rodeos for the money won at this even to count towards 2026 World standings or the 2026 Rookie of the Year standings. Money will count towards circuit standings and this event will be applied towards a circuit count. Money won at this event will not count toward All Around standings.
STK CONT.: Various

The contestants with the top 12 fastest times from the first go-round will be placed in the performance (slowest time will run first, fastest time will run last). The number of contestants placed in the performance will not exceed 12. If splits result in more than 12, a random draw will determine which contestants will compete in the performance and which will compete in the slack. The order of competition of ties from the first go-round will also be determined by random draw. If there are not 12 qualified times from the first go-round to fill the performance, the remaining positions will be filled by contestants based on the reverse order of their first go-round positions (only contestants who competed in the first go-round will be placed in the performances). The remaining contestants (not placed in the performance) will run their second go-round in reverse order of their first go-round positions. The order of the draw will be the same as the competition order. The second go-round will begin in the slack, immediately following the competition of the first go-round.

The second go-round for that group will be run after the SW and TD and will be followed by the TR slack. The top ten SR contestants based on the average after the first two go-rounds will compete during the performance that same night for their third go-round, and the remainder will run their third go-round during slack that same day after all other slack events are completed. Extras will be used to replace sick or injured animals. The misdraw procedure will not be used. Stock charge $80 per go-round.

GROUND RULES: ALL CONTESTANTS - May also enter online at www.rodeocanda.com between June 7 at 8 AM and June 8 at 2 PM.
ALL CONTESTANTS - A maximum of twelve (12) contestants will be drawn into the first (1st) performance at 6:30 PM on Monday June 25th.
ALL CONTESTANTS - Timed Event slack 9:30 am MST each morning.
PAYOUT - SW, TDR, TR payout will be 8 placings in go-rounds and aggregate. BB, SB, BR as per CPRA rulebook.
FORMAT: SB, BB, BR - 1 full go-round, with finals (12), top 4 showdown round.
TDR, SW, TR - 2 full go-rounds with finals (12), top 4 showdown.

TE - Timed Events first go-round run will be in the slack, each morning. Second go-round run will be in the afternoon performance, the same day. (ie., if a contestant is up in the first slack for his go-round run, he will be up in the first performance for his second go-round run). In the Timed Events in case of a foul/re-run, spare will be used.
TR - There will be a maximum of twelve (12) teams per performance. Both members of the team must be full members and/or Semi Pro.
Qualifications TDR & SW - Full & Semi Pro Members ONLY: Maximum 72 based on 75 CPRA/PRCA standings as of May 27, 2026.

Qualifications TR - Full & Semi Pro Members ONLY: Top 72 based off combined 75 CPRA/PRCA standings as of May 27, 2026. If more than 72 teams qualify from above then contestants with the least amount of money won from the 2025 season will be drawn out. If teams are drawn out, only teams that are both full members will remain entered.

Qualifications SB, BB, & BR - Full member, Semi Pro, and permits: Top 72 based on combined CPRA/PRCA standings as of May 27, 2026. If more than 72 contestants qualify from the above, then the contestants with the least amount of money won from the 2025 season, and up to and including May 27, 2026 will be drawn out.

TURN-OUT/ ALTERNATE PROCEDURE: If more than 72 entries contestants drawn out of the pool will be numbered as drawn out. (Ie: First drawn out will be number one, second drawn out will be number two etc.) This will be the order of alternate contestants. Contestants will be notified of there alternate position number at call back at which time they must provide their contact information to be eligible for re-entry. If or when a contestant turns-out the next alternate available will be contacted for re-entry.

MEDICAL EXEMPTION - Consideration will be given to those members who qualified in 2025 but because of injures were unable to compete at any rodeos after July 1, 2025. A letter on doctor's letterhead must be submitted to the CRES office prior to entries opening, this letter must detail the time frame in which contestant was unable to compete. Injury information must be given to CRES at the time of entry.
PLEASE NOTE - Section VII A. 1 & 3 and Section VIII A 13 of the CPRA rulebook will be strictly enforced by the Pro Rodeo Officials.
FINALS - $5,000 will be held out in each of the seven major events for the finals. Four (4) monies will be paid in the finals. Split 40-30-20-10.

TD, SW, TR - Top twelve (12), if a tie exists, it will be broken by the fastest time on any one head. If still tied, the tie will be broken by the second fastest time on any one head. If still tied the Canadian Standings as of June 18, 2025 will be the tie breaker.

SB, BB, BR - Top twelve (12), if a tie exists, it will be broken by going back to judge's card, the high mark contestant on the cowboy spur ride will break the tie. If still tied the Canadian Standings as of June 18, 2026 will be the tie breaker.

TURNING OUT FINALS - Contestants who turn-out of the Finals must notify the local Rodeo Office by Tuesday, June 30 no later than 6 PM MST. A $500 turn out fine will apply if the contestant fails to notify by the specified time. Contestants who are a notified turn-out or contestants who are unavailable at the start of the section of their event will be replaced by the next available contestant; next is defined by the 2026 Ponoka Stampede standings. Ponoka Stampede reserves the right to roll contestants into the Finals (to total of 12 contestants) in the event of turn outs. In case of ties between 13-14 etc., tie breaker rules to decide the next contestant into the finals, the procedure will be the same as determining the top twelve (12) qualifiers.

SHOWDOWN FORMAT - Cowboy Rule - Must make a qualified ride or run to be paid. NO GROUND MONEY WILL BE PAID. All monies paid in the SHOWDOWN will count towards CPRA/PRCA standings. In the event no qualified rides/times in the showdown there will no payout and the average winner will be the Stampede Champion. The Showdown prize money will be carried forward to the next year's Showdown, split with the same percentages as regular Showdown pay-out and will count for CPRA/PRCA standings. No times or score will be carried into the Showdown. All stock will be selected by the event reps and the committee. Order of competition will be fourth (4th) to first (1st), timed events must be split so as no back to back runs on the same horse. Top four (4) contestants, maximum of four (4), from the average of the rodeo will compete in the Showdown. If not enough qualified rides/runs for the Showdown, the highest score taken to the Finals will qualify (also includes injuries).
PRIZE MONEY - $15,000, held out per event for the Showdown split as follows:
Four (4) Qualified Rides/Runs:
Three (3) Qualified Rides/Runs:
Two (2) Qualified Rides/Runs:
One (1) Qualified Ride/Run:

TIE BREAKER FORMAT TO QUALIFY FOR SHOWDOWN - SB, BB, BR - Highest score on the Finals will break ties. If a tie still exists the contestant with the highest score in the first (1st) go-round will break the tie. If a tie still exists, the contestant with the most money won in previous go-rounds on two (2) head will advance. If a tie still exists, the highest marked spur ride on the judges' cards from the Finals (top 12) will proceed. If a tie till exists the Canadian Standings as of June 18, 2026 will be used.

TD, SW, TR - Fastest time in the Finals will break ties. If a ties still exists the fastest time in the first (1st) go-round will break the tie. If a tie still exists the contestant with the most money won in previous go-rounds on two (2) head will advance. If a tie still exists, the Canadian Standings as of June 18, 2026 will be used.

SHOWDOWN TIE BREAKERS - All tie breakers are based on qualified rides and times only. If a tie exists after the showdown contestants have competed once, there will be either a ride off or run off (depending on the event) between the tied contestants to determine the Champion. In rough stock events, if a ride off is required, any animals that were drawn as re-rides for the Finals and were not used will automatically be the ride-off animals. In timed events, if a run off is required, the designated spares will be used as the tie breaker animals. If a tie still exists after a ride off/run off, contestants will be co-champions.
STK CONT.: Wayne Vold Rodeo

GROUND RULES: Contestants who choose to enter the Legacy Steer Roping event must be at least 50 years old or a permit holder at the time of entry closing. They must also be entered in the steer roping event at the World's Oldest Rodeo. To be eligible, the contestant must not have been an NFSR qualifier during the past 3 years. Permit members of all ages will also be eligible to enter.

Contestants will pay an additional entry fees of $300. Contestants will not compete on any additional steers. The times that are recorded for the contestants' competition runs at the World's Oldest Rodeo will be used to determine the pay-off. Pay-off will only include the entry fees for the contestants who entered the Legacy Steer Roping through PROCOM. 6% will be held out of the total amount for the PRCA prior to the pay-off. Only the three go-rounds and the average after three go-rounds will be included in the pay-off for the Legacy Steer Roping. There will be no additional added money and since no additional animals will be run, there will be no additional stock charge or PROCOM charge.

Money won in the Legacy Steer Roping will not count towards PRCA World Standings, circuit standings, All Around standings, or for money won qualifications. It will count towards qualifying for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals held in conjunction with the National Finals Steer Roping. (NFSR qualifiers will not be eligible for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals).
STK CONT.: Various
